record.original_question: For the graph-model version of Isaacs' princess and monster game, where the searcher finds the hider once they are in the same place, solve the game on graphs other than the circle. In particular, determine the correct solution for the interval case, which the source says is not solved but only conjectured.

evidence.quote: The searcher then ﬁnds the hider once they are in the same place. This version of the princess and monster game was also proposed by Isaacs [11, p 349-350]. The game on a graph has only been solved for the circle (see Sect. 1.2 of this book), but it remains open for all other graphs. Even if the graph is an interval, although there is a conjectured solution in this case, which we will discuss below.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following zero-sum pursuit-evasion game (the "princess and monster" game) played on a connected graph G = (V, E) whose edges are isometric to closed intervals of given positive lengths, equipped with the induced shortest-path metric. Two players, a Searcher S (the monster) and a Hider H (the princess), each move continuously along G with speed at most 1. The game takes place in continuous time t ≥ 0. At t = 0 each player independently chooses a (possibly randomized) starting point in G, and thereafter each player chooses a (measurable) trajectory of speed at most 1; the Searcher does not see the Hider's position and the Hider does not see the Searcher's position. The capture time T is the first time t ≥ 0 at which the two players occupy the same point of G. The Searcher seeks to minimize, and the Hider to maximize, the expected capture time E[T]. Let V(G) denote the value of this game.

(a) For graphs G other than a single circle (a graph isometric to a circle of given total length L, for which the value is known to equal L/2 times an established constant), determine V(G) and optimal strategies for both players.

(b) In particular, solve the case in which G is a closed interval [0, 1] of length 1: determine the exact value V([0,1]) and exhibit optimal (or ε-optimal) mixed strategies for both the Searcher and the Hider.
artifact.status_search_result: The princess-and-monster game on a graph has been solved only for the circle. For the interval, Alpern, Fokkink, Lindelauf, and Olsder (SIAM J. Control Optim., 2008) showed the value V satisfies 15/11 ≤ V ≤ 13/9 (with V < 3/2), and derived properties of optimal strategies, but the exact value and optimal strategies remain unknown. No complete solution for the interval, or for general graphs, appears in the literature, so the problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: The 'Princess and Monster' Game on an Interval
status_evidence.snippet: Showed 15/11 ≤ V ≤ 13/9 and V < 3/2 for the interval case, with optimal strategy properties but no closed-form value.
status_evidence.claim: Only bounds (not exact value) are established for the interval; problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Princess and monster game - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The game has been solved by Shmuel Gal for a circle; the case of a general multidimensional region remains unsolved.
status_evidence.claim: Only the circle case has a complete solution.

status_evidence.title: The princess and monster game on the circle and the interval (van Laere thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews known bounds for the interval and notes the exact value is not known.
status_evidence.claim: The interval case remains open up to bounds.
